'''Tibor Gallai''' (born Tibor Grünwald, 15 July 1912 – 2 January 1992) was a [[Hungarians|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]]. He worked in [[combinatorics]], especially in [[graph theory]], and  was a lifelong friend and collaborator of [[Paul Erdős]].  He was a student of [[Dénes Kőnig]] and an advisor of [[László Lovász]]. He was a corresponding member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (1991).

== His main results ==
The [[Edmonds&ndash;Gallai decomposition theorem]], which was proved independently by Gallai and [[Jack Edmonds]], describes finite graphs from the point of view of matchings. Gallai also proved, with [[Arthur Milgram|Milgram]], [[Dilworth's theorem]] in 1947, but as they hesitated to publish the result, Dilworth independently discovered and published it.<ref>P. Erdős: [https://doi.org/10.1007%2FBF01305229 In memory of Tibor Gallai], ''[[Combinatorica]]'', '''12'''(1992), 373&ndash;374.</ref>

Gallai was the first to prove the higher-dimensional version of [[van der Waerden's theorem]].

With [[Paul Erdős]] he gave a [[necessary and sufficient condition]] for a sequence to be the degree sequence of a graph, known as the [[Erdős–Gallai theorem]].
